name: Kerala-style fish curry with brown rice
steps: Simmer the fish gently in the coconut milk with tamarind paste, turmeric, and chilli until just cooked through.
Cook the brown rice according to pack instructions.
Serve the fish curry hot over the rice.

name: Sambar with brown rice and cabbage thoran
steps: Simmer the red lentils with the mixed vegetables and tamarind paste until soft for the sambar.
Stir-fry the cabbage with desiccated coconut and mustard seeds for the thoran.
Cook the brown rice and serve with the sambar and thoran.

name: Avial with rice
steps: Simmer the mixed vegetables until just tender.
Blend the coconut with cumin and green chilli, stir through the vegetables with the yoghurt, and warm gently without boiling.
Serve the avial with the cooked brown rice.

name: Kerala-style chicken curry with rice and spinach
steps: Fry the sliced onion with curry leaves and Kerala spices until soft.
Add the chicken and coconut milk, and simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Stir in the spinach for the last few minutes and serve hot with the cooked brown rice.

name: Varan bhaat with spinach bhaji
steps: Simmer the red lentils until soft, then season simply with turmeric and a little ghee for the varan.
Stir-fry the spinach with mustard seeds and garlic for the bhaji.
Serve the varan over the cooked brown rice with the bhaji alongside.

name: Misal pav
steps: Simmer the sprouted bean mix with the onion and warming spices until tender.
Ladle the curry into a bowl and scatter the crushed peanuts over the top.
Serve with the warmed wholemeal bread roll.

name: Pithla with wholemeal bhakri
steps: Whisk the besan with water, garlic, and onion, and cook over a low heat, stirring, until thick and glossy for the pithla.
Knead the wholemeal flour with warm water and pat into a flatbread; cook on a hot griddle until speckled for the bhakri.
Serve the pithla hot with the bhakri.

name: Amti with rice
steps: Simmer the red lentils until soft.
Stir in the tamarind paste, honey, and garam masala, and simmer a few minutes more for the amti.
Serve hot over the cooked brown rice.
